paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across nine language families, with error bars denoting standard deviation, and compares six multilingual BERT model configurations: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light pink), and XLM-B2 (red). The horizontal axis categorizes language families in the order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 30 with major tick marks at intervals of 10, representing the magnitude of masking impact on case prediction performance. Across all families, IE-Indic exhibits the highest effects, with most models scoring between 17 and 25, particularly XLM-R2 and XLM-B2 reaching approximately 23–24. In contrast, Isolate and Uralic families show near-zero effects across all models, with bars clustered around 0–2. IE-Germanic consistently outperforms IE-Romance, with XLM-B2 reaching ~20 in Germanic versus ~13 in Romance. For IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) show effects roughly twice those of L2 and R2 variants, with B2 bars reaching ~16–17. Semitic displays the largest error bars, indicating high variability, with mBERT-L2 achieving ~15. The bars are grouped by language family, with each group containing six bars ordered by model type, and no sorting by effect size is applied within groups. Some bars, such as those for Semitic and IE-Indic, are notably taller and accompanied by larger error bars, visually emphasizing greater performance and variability in those families.
